claims.content: To capture information when a distributor is planning to return the vouchers back to the MSIU sales team.

goal.raw_text: To capture information when a distributor is planning to return the vouchers back to the MSIU sales team.

claims.content: VMU User
The VMU User must be authenticated with a valid User Name and Password to access the system.
The VMU User must have the necessary Security and User Privileges to access the 'Voucher Sales Return' module.
The system must be running on the Oracle 9i platform with the Visual Basic front end available.
A distributor decides to return vouchers back to the MSIU sales team.

trigger.raw_text: A distributor decides to return vouchers back to the MSIU sales team.

claims.content: The VMU User initiates the Voucher Sales Return transaction.
The system captures the Distributor Name, listing it from the Distributor Master.
The system captures the Sales Man Name, listing it from the Sales Man Master.
The system captures the Sales Return Date, defaulting to the system date (which must be less than or equal to the current system date).
The system captures the Number of vouchers Returned.
The system calculates and captures the Sales Return Amount based on the formula: No of voucher returned x whole sale rate.
The user enters the Batch No for the transaction part.
The user enters the Voucher No for the transaction part.
The system validates that all above information is mandatory before saving.
If the user attempts to save a record with an existing Distributor Name, the system will give a warning message to have the duplicate name or to change the name.
The system will not allow the user to create a User Group and Individual User with existing names.
Deleting records will be allowed only if no child records are created.
If the user enters a Sales Return Date that is greater than the system date, the system will not accept the entry.
If the Password and Verify Password values are not equal during user creation or modification related to the transaction, the system will not save the user information.
If any mandatory field (Distributor Name, Sales Man Name, Sales Return Date, Number of vouchers Returned, Batch No, Voucher No) is left blank, the system will prevent saving the record.
The voucher sales return transaction is recorded in the system database with all mandatory fields populated.
The system updates the distributor’s sales history to reflect the returned quantity and adjusted balance.
The system ensures that no duplicate user or group names are created during any associated user management actions related to the return process.
The system maintains data integrity by preventing deletion of records if child records exist, ensuring auditability of returns.
